ALG-H4-11.new_tell: Three of the four options (42, 48, 54) form an arithmetic run with common difference 6 and 30 is the lone outlier, so a blind solver discards 30 on shape alone and guesses 1-in-3. Mitigating: all four are multiples of 6 and all four are positive integers, so the key is not the odd one out by shape or sign, and the spread 30-54 does not leak the scale beyond what the stem already fixes (the larger number must lie in [30, 60)).
ALG-H4-11.note: Domain check passes and is the item's strongest feature. The maximum is genuinely attained: at s = 18 the constraint holds with equality (54 = 42 + 12), so the greatest value exists rather than being a supremum. It is also invariant to the two readings a solver might take - imposing the implied ordering L >= s or ignoring it both give 3(60 - L) >= L + 12 -> L <= 42 - and invariant to whether the numbers are integers or reals. So there is no unstated-domain hole and no second route to any option. The nearest thing to a two-route option is 30: it is both the minimum of the larger number and the equal-split value, but neither reading answers 'greatest', so it is not defensible. Distractors: 48 (attaching the 12 to the wrong side) is the strong one and is exactly the trap the stem is built around; 54 (reporting 3s, the compared quantity, instead of 60 - s) is a real slip; 30 is close to filler but is not eliminable by kind or magnitude - it sits inside the range the stem fixes and is the correct sort of quantity, so the set stays legal. Not weak. Difficulty is medium rather than hard: it is one translation (at-least, correct side) plus one substitution plus a boundary check, with no second concept layered on. A strong student on the module-2 hard route is not detained by it; hard on that route means the item resists a correct first move, and this one rewards the first move.

ALG-H4-22.new_tell: The option set is 1, 2, 3, 4 - a fully consecutive run starting at the stem's own lower bound. That is maximally regular and it leaks the scale: it announces that the answer is a small count, and a blind solver who takes a middle value has a 50% shot. The key, 3, is also 'one less than the largest option', a common shape for strict-inequality counting items. I cannot attribute this to the repair (I did not read the prior version), but it is the one thing in either item I would change: replacing 1 with a larger non-adjacent count would break the run without making any option illegal.
ALG-H4-22.note: The unbounded-domain check is the thing to test here and it passes. The counted set is bounded below by the stem ('m is at least 1', 'whole-number') and bounded above by the inequality itself (60 + 45m > 60m -> m < 4), so the count is finite without needing any unstated cap. The joining fee is explicitly 'one-time', so total cost at club 1 is unambiguously 60 + 45m rather than 60 per month plus 45. Strictness is clean: 'greater than' excludes m = 4, where both totals are 240 and neither club is more expensive - there is no reading of 'greater' that admits equality, so 4 is an error path only and not a second defensible answer. No option is reachable by two routes. Distractor quality: every option is a legal count, so not weak by kind or magnitude, and each error path is a real one (rate-difference confusion for 1, off-by-one start for 2, non-strict inequality for 4). But 1 is nearly self-eliminating - checking m = 2 (150 vs 120) is two multiplications and no algebra - which keeps this at plausible rather than strong. Difficulty is medium, at the low end: setting up 60 + 45m > 60m is a single step, the arithmetic reduces to 60 > 15m, and the only real demand is remembering to count integers instead of reporting the crossing point.
